`Game` gains a `requirements` slot: the `RequirementRegistry` from `core-requirement`, built with the game's own `RuleRegistry` so the rules its entries make always go into the same game. `defaultGame` adopts the module `instance`, which is built with `core-rule`'s (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).

A `Requirement` is one edge of a ruleset's graph: a subject, a relation (`requires`, `excludedBy`, `obsoletedBy`, `replacedBy`, or one a plugin declares), its targets, how they combine and whose possession counts. `RequirementRegistry` holds a game's entries and registers the rules each owning package's deriver makes from them, under the entries' own ids, so play is unchanged. `replace` and `remove` change an entry and its rules together, and `for`/`leadsTo` read the graph either way for the civilopedia (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
From the review of civ-clone/web-renderer#37's first batch:

`add` and `replace` check everything before changing anything: duplicate entry ids (including two replacements under one id), rule ids another rule already has, and entries that aren't entries. A plain object is taken as an entry, as a plugin might write one.

An entry owns the ids of the rules it made: replacing or removing it takes out whatever rule holds them by then, including one a plugin put in their place with `rules.replace`, so the last change wins.
`unregister` removes the entries it holds, by identity, and ignores others, like any registry.
Entries are frozen, since a ruleset's are shared by every game and its rules read them as they run.
`ruleRegistry()` says which rule registry the entries' rules go into.

core-rule 0.1.5 is the first with rule ids (`getById`, `DuplicateRuleIdError`), and the tests pass against 0.1.5 of both. Requiring ^0.1.6 put a second core-rule beside a tree that had settled on 0.1.5 (core-save-game's CI), so a game's rules and its requirements' were two different `RuleRegistry` classes.

`requirements` (core-game's new slot) is dispositioned `definitions`: plugin imports register its entries along with their rules, and play never changes them, so a load adopts it with `rules` and a save writes none of it (civ-clone/web-renderer#37).
